original_question: For an infinite word u, let Ru(n) be the size of the smallest window that contains every factor of length n of u, and define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = lim sup_{n->infinity} Ru(n)/n. How does this recurrence quotient behave for families of infinite words beyond Sturmian words, such as words of complexity 2n + 1, or even for more general infinite words?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Question 2.1.97.2 (“The recurrence quotient”; WORDS 1997, Julien Cassaigne). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.04055))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it uses the recurrence-function/recurrence-quotient setup, keeps the focus on families other than Sturmian words, and retains the paper’s two explicit examples, namely words of complexity 2n + 1 and infinite words in general. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.04055))
missing_details: Define factor complexity explicitly: p_u(n) should be the number of distinct factors of u of length n; otherwise “words of complexity 2n + 1” is not fully stand-alone.
Specify the ambient object: u should be an infinite word over a finite alphabet.
Clarify that a “window” is a factor of u.
If the Sturmian benchmark is mentioned explicitly, note the nearby paper notation: for a Sturmian sequence of irrational slope α, the recurrence quotient is denoted ρ(α).
Keep the scope at the paper’s level: it asks for a study of recurrence quotients for other families, not necessarily a complete classification or exact formula.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; those notions are inapplicable to this combinatorics-on-words problem.
refined_question: Let u be an infinite word over a finite alphabet, let p_u(n) denote the number of distinct factors of u of length n, let R_u(n) be the length of the smallest factor (window) of u containing every factor of u of length n, and define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = limsup_{n→∞} R_u(n)/n. Beyond the Sturmian case, develop a study of recurrence quotients for other families of infinite words, in particular for words whose factor complexity satisfies p_u(n) = 2n + 1, and more generally for infinite words in general.
justification: The draft is not aiming at any statement labeled Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; it matches the open problem in Section 2.1. There the paper first introduces the recurrence function, then defines the recurrence quotient ρ(u), recalls the Sturmian notation ρ(α), and immediately asks for a study of recurrence quotients beyond Sturmian words, explicitly pointing to words of complexity 2n + 1 and to infinite words in general. The refinement above stays as close as possible to that official formulation while only adding the minimum notation needed to make the question self-contained, chiefly p_u(n) for factor complexity and the clarification that a window is a factor of u. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.04055))
